edges.description: Truncated and disulphide-disrupted FXIII-B is retained in the secretory pathway instead of being released.
Little or no FXIII-B reaches plasma.
Without its carrier, FXIII-A2 is removed from the circulation faster, producing a secondary A-subunit deficiency.
FXIII-B also links the FXIII zymogen to fibrinogen, so its absence slows activation of whatever FXIII-A remains.
edges.target: Impaired Thrombin Activation of FXIII-A on Fibrin

edges.description: Less FXIII-A in plasma means less activatable transglutaminase.
Slower activation delays cross-linking of the fibrin clot.
edges.source: Impaired Thrombin Activation of FXIII-A on Fibrin

edges.description: Less transglutaminase activity means less fibrin cross-linking.
The same loss of transglutaminase activity also leaves less alpha-2-antiplasmin covalently ligated into the clot, which is a separate substrate from the fibrin chains themselves.
A clot carrying less covalently bound inhibitor is lysed sooner.
edges.target: Accelerated Fibrinolysis of the Formed Clot

edges.description: Premature lysis of an adequate clot produces delayed bleeding.
edges.source: Accelerated Fibrinolysis of the Formed Clot

edges.description: An unstable clot gives a bleeding tendency.
Deep soft-tissue bleeding is the reported spontaneous bleed.
Mucosal bleeding is reported in the same patient.
Low plasma FXIII-A that is corrected by restoring FXIII-B, reproducing the secondary A-subunit deficiency.
Reduced plasma cross-linking and prolonged bleeding time.
edges.limitations: Bleeding time in mice is a tail-transection measure and does not map directly onto the provoked mucosal and soft-tissue bleeding reported in patients.

nodes.description: A bleeding tendency that is milder than in A-subunit deficiency and can be brought out by an acquired condition. Some individuals come to attention only in adulthood.

evidence.reference_title: Factor XIII Deficiency: Laboratory, Molecular, and Clinical Aspects.
evidence.snippet: patients with severe FXIII-B deficiency present with a milder phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Alloantibodies against the B subunit of plasma factor XIII developed in its congenital deficiency.
evidence.snippet: An originally mild bleeding phenotype of severe congenital FXIII-B deficiency can be exaggerated by additional acquired conditions.

nodes.description: Plasma FXIII-B is undetectable or severely reduced, so FXIII-A2 cannot form the stable A2B2 heterotetramer.

evidence.reference_title: Alloantibodies against the B subunit of plasma factor XIII developed in its congenital deficiency.
evidence.snippet: At the age of 74, ELISA and western blotting assay unexpectedly revealed complete absence of FXIII-B in the patient's plasma.

evidence.reference_title: Type I factor XIII deficiency is caused by a genetic defect of its b subunit: insertion of triplet AAC in exon III leads to premature termination in the second Sushi domain.
evidence.snippet: there were normal amounts of the mutant mRNA, but no b subunit was detected in these patients.

nodes.description: Premature plasmin-mediated dissolution of a clot that formed normally. This is the second route to the bleeding phenotype and is mechanistically distinct from the mechanically weak clot: here the clot is lysed too soon rather than being too fragile. It is an inference from the substrate biology rather than a measurement in this disease, and is recorded as such.
nodes.id: Accelerated Fibrinolysis of the Formed Clot

evidence.reference_title: Coagulation factor XIII: a multifunctional transglutaminase with clinical potential in a range of conditions.
evidence.snippet: being the principal mechanism(s) whereby plasmin-mediated clot degradation is minimised

nodes.description: Secondary FXIII-A deficiency. F13A1 and platelet FXIII-A are normal, but plasma FXIII-A falls because the uncomplexed A2 dimer has a shorter circulating life than the A2B2 heterotetramer. The subunits stabilise each other: free FXIII-B2 is also cleared faster than complexed FXIII-B2.

animal_models.description: Low plasma FXIII-A that is corrected by restoring FXIII-B, reproducing the secondary A-subunit deficiency.
animal_models.name: FXIII-B knockout mouse (F13b-/-)

evidence.reference_title: Type I factor XIII deficiency is caused by a genetic defect of its b subunit: insertion of triplet AAC in exon III leads to premature termination in the second Sushi domain.
evidence.snippet: The a subunit deficiency of these patients must be a secondary to the b subunit deficiency, as their gene for the a subunit was intact, and the a subunit in their platelets was present within normal levels.

evidence.reference_title: Reciprocal stabilization of coagulation factor XIII-A and -B subunits is a determinant of plasma FXIII concentration.
evidence.snippet: comparison of free FXIII-B2 vs FXIII-A2-complexed FXIII-B2 (FXIII-A2B2) infused into mice revealed faster clearance of free FXIII-B2.

nodes.description: Homozygous or compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in F13B, which encodes the B subunit of factor XIII, a protein built from ten sushi domains held together by disulphide bonds. Reported variants include premature-termination alleles (the AAC insertion at Tyr-80 that is a founder allele in Italian families, and a splice-boundary deletion that is a founder allele in Japanese families), frameshifts, and missense variants that remove or sit next to a structural disulphide bond. Most of them reduce the amount of FXIII-B that leaves the cell rather than producing a secreted but inactive protein.

evidence.reference_title: Type I factor XIII deficiency is caused by a genetic defect of its b subunit: insertion of triplet AAC in exon III leads to premature termination in the second Sushi domain.
evidence.snippet: DNA sequence analysis showed that a nucleotide triplet (AAC) was inserted within the codon for Tyr-80 in exon III of the gene for a female proband's b subunit, resulting in the creation of a stop codon.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations affecting disulphide bonds contribute to a fairly common prevalence of F13B gene defects: results of a genetic study in 14 families with factor XIII B deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Two of the missense mutations (Cys5Arg, Cys316Phe) eliminated disulphide bonds (Cys5-Cys56, Cys316-Cys358).

evidence.reference_title: Factor XIII: novel structural and functional aspects.
evidence.snippet: FXIII-B is a glycoprotein consisting of 10 repetitive sushi domains each held together by two internal disulfide bonds.

evidence.reference_title: A founder effect is proposed for factor XIII B subunit deficiency caused by the insertion of triplet AAC in exon III encoding the second Sushi domain.
evidence.snippet: suggesting that a founder effect is responsible for factor XIII B subunit deficiency in Italians.

evidence.reference_title: Truncated mutant B subunit for factor XIII causes its deficiency due to impaired intracellular transportation.
evidence.snippet: Both patients have a previously described one-base deletion at the boundary between intron A/exon II in the XIIIB gene, heterozygously or homozygously.

nodes.description: Gene-targeted mice lacking FXIII-B are viable and fertile, have prolonged bleeding times, and show markedly reduced but detectable plasma cross-linking activity. Infusing recombinant human FXIII-B raises their plasma FXIII-A. Older male knockouts develop mild cardiac fibrosis with haemosiderin deposits, without the fatal cardiac haemorrhage seen in FXIII-A knockout males.
Gingival bleeding, reported in the same patient at the same time as thrombocytopenia, which may have contributed.

evidence.reference_title: Alloantibodies against the B subunit of plasma factor XIII developed in its congenital deficiency.
evidence.snippet: He developed thrombocytopenia and gingival bleedings at the age of 73

nodes.description: Alpha-2-antiplasmin is the other principal haemostatic substrate of activated FXIII, and cross-linking it into fibrin is the main way a clot resists plasmin. With less transglutaminase activity, less inhibitor is ligated. This arm is modelled because it follows from the reduced FXIIIa activity this entry already asserts, not from anything A-subunit specific; it has not been measured in a B-subunit-deficient patient.

evidence.reference_title: Coagulation factor XIII: a multifunctional transglutaminase with clinical potential in a range of conditions.
evidence.snippet: These include antifibrinolytic proteins, with cross-linking of α2-antiplasmin to fibrin, and potentially fibrinogen, being the principal mechanism(s) whereby plasmin-mediated clot degradation is minimised

nodes.description: FXIII-B is synthesised by hepatocytes. Mutant FXIII-B is held in the endoplasmic reticulum or fails to reach the Golgi apparatus, so little or none is released into plasma. Secretion deficits were found for every patient-derived missense variant tested in one cell expression study, though a follow-up study found that several of those variants act mainly by reducing protein stability or binding to FXIII-A.

biological_processes: endoplasmic reticulum to Golgi vesicle-mediated transport

evidence.reference_title: Reciprocal stabilization of coagulation factor XIII-A and -B subunits is a determinant of plasma FXIII concentration.
evidence.snippet: Plasma FXIII is composed of A and B subunit dimers synthesized in cells of hematopoietic origin and hepatocytes, respectively.

evidence.reference_title: In vitro secretion deficits are common among human coagulation factor XIII subunit B missense mutants: correlations with patient phenotypes and molecular models.
evidence.snippet: In vitro expression of FXIII B subunit (FXIIIB) missense variants in HEK293T cells revealed impaired secretion for all seven variants studied.

evidence.reference_title: Truncated mutant B subunit for factor XIII causes its deficiency due to impaired intracellular transportation.
evidence.snippet: immunocytochemical examinations by epifluorescence, confocal, and electron microscopes indicated impaired intracellular transportation of the truncated XIIIB from the endoplasmic reticulum to the Golgi apparatus.

evidence.reference_title: Structural and functional influences of coagulation factor XIII subunit B heterozygous missense mutants.
evidence.snippet: The Cys5Arg mutation was the only mutation to show a direct secretion-based defect since the mutated protein was observed to accumulate in the endoplasmic reticulum.

nodes.description: Fibrin gamma- and alpha-chain isopeptide cross-linking is slower and less complete, giving a mechanically weaker clot. Both upstream routes, loss of FXIII-A by clearance and slower activation of what remains, converge here.

animal_models.description: Reduced plasma cross-linking and prolonged bleeding time.
animal_models.name: FXIII-B knockout mouse (F13b-/-)

biological_processes: fibrin gamma- and alpha-chain isopeptide cross-linking

evidence.reference_title: Administration of factor XIII B subunit increased plasma factor XIII A subunit levels in factor XIII B subunit knock-out mice.
evidence.snippet: thrombin-dependent amine incorporation and fibrin-crosslinking in plasma were undetectable in the FXIII-A-deficient mice and markedly reduced in the FXIII-B-deficient mice

evidence.reference_title: The Non-catalytic B Subunit of Coagulation Factor XIII Accelerates Fibrin Cross-linking.
evidence.snippet: congenital or acquired FXIII-B deficiency may result in increased bleeding tendency through impaired fibrin stabilization due to decreased FXIII-A activation by thrombin and secondary FXIII-A deficiency arising from enhanced circulatory clearance.

nodes.description: FXIII-B binds fibrinogen and brings proenzyme FXIII, fibrinogen and thrombin together. Without it, thrombin cleavage of the FXIII-A activation peptide and FXIII-A incorporation into the clot are both slower.
nodes.id: Impaired Thrombin Activation of FXIII-A on Fibrin

evidence.reference_title: The Non-catalytic B Subunit of Coagulation Factor XIII Accelerates Fibrin Cross-linking.
evidence.snippet: Immunoprecipitation with an anti-fibrinogen antibody revealed an interaction between the FXIII heterotetramer and fibrinogen mediated by FXIII-B and not FXIII-A.

evidence.reference_title: Factor XIII: novel structural and functional aspects.
evidence.snippet: In the circulation pFXIII is bound to the fibrinogen γ'-chain through its B subunit.

evidence.reference_title: Factor XIII: novel structural and functional aspects.
evidence.snippet: In the process of pFXIII activation first thrombin cleaves off the activation peptide from FXIII-A, then in the presence of Ca(2+) FXIII-B dissociates and FXIII-A becomes transformed into an active transglutaminase (FXIIIa). The activation is highly accelerated by the presence of fibrin(ogen).

nodes.description: Spontaneous intramuscular haematoma, reported in an older adult with severe deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Alloantibodies against the B subunit of plasma factor XIII developed in its congenital deficiency.
evidence.snippet: When he suddenly developed spontaneous intramuscular haematoma, the bleeding was arrested by infusing FXIII concentrates.

nodes.description: Plasma-derived FXIII concentrate contains both subunits and is the replacement product for B-subunit deficiency. Because the phenotype is mild, patients may need it only on demand for bleeding or before surgery rather than as routine prophylaxis. Recombinant FXIII-A2 (catridecacog), the prophylactic product used for A-subunit deficiency, is not appropriate here, because it supplies no FXIII-B. Repeated concentrate infusion led to anti-FXIII-B alloantibodies in one patient with complete absence of FXIII-B, after which replacement became less effective.

evidence.reference_title: Factor XIII Deficiency: A Review of Biology, Testing, and Treatment.
evidence.snippet: recombinant FXIII-A2 is appropriate for F13A1 defects but not patients with F13B variants.

evidence.reference_title: Factor XIII Deficiency: Laboratory, Molecular, and Clinical Aspects.
evidence.snippet: patients with severe FXIII-B deficiency may only require on-demand therapy, while heterozygotes are generally asymptomatic.

evidence.reference_title: Alloantibodies against the B subunit of plasma factor XIII developed in its congenital deficiency.
evidence.snippet: Repeated infusions of exogenous FXIII for hemostasis increased anti-FXIII-B alloantibodies that resisted FXIII substitution.

nodes.description: Plasma FXIII activity is reduced, to about ten percent of normal in the best-described severe case, rather than being absent as in severe A-subunit deficiency. The residual activity is one likely reason the bleeding phenotype is milder.

evidence.reference_title: Alloantibodies against the B subunit of plasma factor XIII developed in its congenital deficiency.
evidence.snippet: his FXIII activity was as low as 10% of the normal.
